ground_truth: Cyst formation in a persistent thyroglossal duct

differential: Thyroid nodule
A lump on the front of the neck in a young girl is commonly due to a thyroid nodule.
Thyroglossal duct cyst
A midline neck mass in a child is often a thyroglossal duct cyst.
Lymphadenopathy
Enlarged cervical lymph nodes can present as a neck lump.
Goiter
Enlargement of the thyroid gland can present as a neck lump.
Branchial cleft cyst
Although less common, a branchial cleft cyst can present as a neck mass.
Thyroglossal duct cyst
The midline neck mass that moves with swallowing and is located between the hyoid bone and mandible is characteristic of a thyroglossal duct cyst.
Dermoid cyst
A midline neck mass that is fluctuant and minimally mobile could also represent a dermoid cyst, although these typically do not move with swallowing.
Lymphadenopathy
Although less likely due to the midline location and movement with swallowing, lymphadenopathy can present as a neck mass.
Ectopic thyroid tissue
Ectopic thyroid tissue can present as a midline neck mass and may move with swallowing, though it is less common.
Branchial cleft cyst
Typically lateral, a branchial cleft cyst could be considered if the presentation is atypical, though it is less likely due to the midline location.
eliminated: The mass is not consistent with a goiter as it is not associated with thyroid enlargement or dysfunction.
